origins.section: 6.1. A Mastercard Message Is EBCDIC Characters Behind a Binary Bitmap
6.2. A Packager That Reads Its Own Messages Back Proves Nothing
6.3. A Frame Is a Two-Byte Binary Length, Then the Message
6.4. Field 48 Is Read Tag by Tag, and an Unknown Tag Must Not Stop the Message

gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-visa-packager-reuse: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-visa-packager-reuse: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-visa-packager-reuse: 6.1 says the BCD packager writes the MTI as the two bytes 01 00 and an EBCDIC host reads 01 00 70 20 as the MTI and refuses the message.
recorded.prompt:q-round-trip-test: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-round-trip-test: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-round-trip-test: 6.2 shows '5 of 5 fields equal' and says the same wrong class packs and unpacks and the two mistakes cancel.
recorded.prompt:q-length-mismatch: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-length-mismatch: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-length-mismatch: 6.3 says a PostChannel host reads the ASCII digits 30 30 as 12336 and waits for bytes that never come until its read timeout fires.
recorded.prompt:q-new-subelement: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-new-subelement: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-new-subelement: 6.4 shows 'Unsupported sub-field 33 unpacking field 48' and says the packager refuses a tag it has no definition for, and the whole message with it.

gates.says: all 12 of this quiz's discriminating readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-visa-packager-reuse:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-visa-packager-reuse:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-visa-packager-reuse:b: 6.1 says the Visa packager writes numbers in BCD, two digits to a byte, not as ASCII characters.
recorded.prompt:q-visa-packager-reuse:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-visa-packager-reuse:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-visa-packager-reuse:c: 6.1 shows the MTI is numeric and BCD-packed too, so the host already fails at the MTI.
recorded.prompt:q-visa-packager-reuse:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-visa-packager-reuse:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-visa-packager-reuse:d: 6.1 says the Visa packager already writes text in EBCDIC, so the terminal is not ASCII and the MTI is what fails.
recorded.prompt:q-round-trip-test:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-round-trip-test:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-round-trip-test:a: 6.2's '5 of 5 fields equal' shows a wrong class still returns the value that was set.
recorded.prompt:q-round-trip-test:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-round-trip-test:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-round-trip-test:b: 6.2 says a round trip can't catch this and only bytes from outside your code can, so the test never looks at the link's bytes.
recorded.prompt:q-round-trip-test:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-round-trip-test:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-round-trip-test:d: 6.2 shows the packed bytes differ from the sample at byte 54, so the test passes for another reason.
recorded.prompt:q-length-mismatch:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-length-mismatch:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-length-mismatch:b: 6.3 says the binary-length host reads two bytes as 12336, never the four digits as 58.
recorded.prompt:q-length-mismatch:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-length-mismatch:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-length-mismatch:c: 6.3 says the host waits until its read timeout; refusing is what the ASCIIChannel host does.
recorded.prompt:q-length-mismatch:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-length-mismatch:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-length-mismatch:d: 6.3 says the host reads 12336, not 58, and waits rather than refusing.
recorded.prompt:q-new-subelement:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-new-subelement:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-new-subelement:b: 6.4 says the packager finds 42 by its tag wherever it is, so its failure is not about fixed offsets.
recorded.prompt:q-new-subelement:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-new-subelement:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-new-subelement:c: 6.4 says the packager refuses an unknown tag; only declaring every tag keeps unknown ones.
recorded.prompt:q-new-subelement:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-new-subelement:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-new-subelement:d: 6.4 puts the silent misread on the hand-written fixed-offset reader, not the packager.

gates.says: each of the 4 questions keys exactly 1 of its distinct options and every option carries the sentence its reader is shown
each of the 4 questions cites a passage the ledger still digests to the value this exercise was built from
